en.intro: Arjuna now draws the final line, refusing to trade the happiness of kin for the grief of war. Listen for the word that seals his refusal.
en.notice: The word here is swajanam, our own people. Arjuna says that if he kills his own people, he cannot be happy. He does not say he might be sad, he says happiness is impossible, and that is why he refuses to fight.
en.next: Yet even as he refuses, Arjuna sees that his opponents do not see the wrong in destroying a family.
en.meaning: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava?

en.intro: Arjuna now draws the final line, refusing to trade the happiness of kin for the grief of war. Listen for the word that seals his refusal.
en.body: Therefore, we are not fit to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. How could we be happy after killing our relatives, O Madhava? The word here is swajanam, our own people. Arjuna says that if he kills his own people, he cannot be happy. He does not say he might be sad, he says happiness is impossible, and that is why he refuses to fight. Yet even as he refuses, Arjuna sees that his opponents do not see the wrong in destroying a family.
